title: Explicit inverse of the specified derived point-automorphism transport
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$ and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$, $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and let $g:s\to s$ be ANY scheme automorphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the finite constant coefficient sheaf or completed coefficient sheaf $\Lambda_s$, for $\Lambda=A_n$ or $R$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and its ordinary unbounded derived module category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $G=g^{-1}$ with the coefficient action transported by $c_\Lambda^{-1}$, $P=Lg^*$ and $\kappa_N:GN\to PN$ for the SPECIFIED comparison of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. For $\Lambda=A_n$ allow every $N\in D(s_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)$; for $\Lambda=R$ allow every derived-complete $N\in D(s_{\mathrm{proet}},R)$ [def-weil-derived-complete]. No boundedness, constructibility, finite Tor amplitude or Weil structure is required.

Let $U=(s,\mathrm{id})$, $V=(s,g)$, and let $\operatorname{ins}_{g,N}:N(V)\to\Gamma(s,GN)$ be the actual inverse-image colimit coprojection followed by sheafification, termwise on a representative complex, as in [lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural]. Let $E_{g,N}:\Gamma(s,GN)\xrightarrow{\sim}N(V)$ be the evaluation identification of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]. Then $\operatorname{ins}_{g,N}^{-1}=E_{g,N}$, and
$$\rho_{g,N}=\operatorname{res}_{g^{-1}}\circ E_{g,N}:\Gamma(s,GN)\longrightarrow\Gamma(s,N)$$
is the two-sided inverse of $\sigma^g_N=\operatorname{ins}_{g,N}\circ\operatorname{res}_g$. These are $\Lambda$-linear maps and are natural in derived morphisms, with sections taken through the exact derived sections functor [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact].

The specified $\kappa_N$ is invertible. At finite coefficients its inverse $\delta_N$ is represented by $x\otimes b\mapsto c_{A_n}^{-1}(b)x$. Integrally, with the actual completion unit $u_N:N\to\widehat N$ and whole-cone normalization $\theta_{g,N}:PN\xrightarrow{\sim}G\widehat N$ of [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback-comparison-normalization], its inverse is $\delta_N=G(u_N)^{-1}\theta_{g,N}$, as a map of the ENTIRE derived objects. In particular the specified composite
$$t^g_N=\Gamma(s,\kappa_N)\sigma^g_N:\Gamma(s,N)\longrightarrow\Gamma(s,PN)$$
has the two-sided inverse $\rho_{g,N}\Gamma(s,\delta_N)$ in $D(\Lambda)$, natural in $N$.

proof.text: Apply the evaluation isomorphism for the site equivalence to $U$: $(GN)(U)\cong N(V)$. The restriction-naturality lemma identifies the ACTUAL colimit insertion followed by sheafification with the identity in these coordinates. Hence $E_{g,N}\operatorname{ins}_{g,N}=1$ and $\operatorname{ins}_{g,N}E_{g,N}=1$ termwise, and the insertion is invertible with inverse $E_{g,N}$. These identities commute with differentials because evaluation and insertion are natural in the sheaf.

proof.text: In the slice site $g:V\to U$ has inverse $g^{-1}:U\to V$: indeed $g\circ g^{-1}=1_s$ and $1_s\circ g=g$. Contravariant functoriality gives $\operatorname{res}_{g^{-1}}\operatorname{res}_g=1_{N(U)}$ and $\operatorname{res}_g\operatorname{res}_{g^{-1}}=1_{N(V)}$. With $\rho=\operatorname{res}_{g^{-1}}E$ and $\sigma=\operatorname{ins}\operatorname{res}_g$, substitute the insertion identities to obtain $\rho\sigma=1$ and $\sigma\rho=1$. The restriction-naturality lemma makes $\sigma$ $\Lambda$-linear for the transported action, so its inverse $\rho$ is linear: apply $\sigma$ to $\rho(by)$ and $b\rho(y)$ and cancel. Restriction and evaluation are linear over constant scalars as well, so insertion and its inverse have this linearity.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-finite-comparison-complex-isomorphism] to the specified finite comparison on every complex. Its inverse delta is a natural chain map: derive naturality of the comparison from its adjunction-unit section formula, then invert the natural isomorphism. Linearity of delta and the formula kappa(x)=the restricted generator give delta(b times generator(x))=c inverse(b) times x. The two inverse identities are those of this natural isomorphism.

proof.text: Use coefficientDerivedSystemEvaluationCalculus to obtain a coherent calculus S. The existing comparison-naturality theorem supplies a natural theta on all ambient objects with kappa followed by theta equal to G of the actual S.adjunction unit; it packages the normalization lemma without choosing a complete input. The reconstruction theorem makes the unit invertible on every derived-complete N. Hence kappa_N is invertible. Take Delta_N to be its inverse isomorphism, and epsilon_N to be G of the unit isomorphism. Cancellation gives Delta_N.hom=theta_N followed by epsilon_N.inv, and naturality of the inverse follows by cancelling kappa on both sides of its naturality square.

proof.text: Repeat the proved algebraically-closed-field ring-retraction argument with independent site and coefficient universes; this is also the argument of the current point-sections exactness node. Evaluation preserves epimorphisms by the affine weak-contractibility theorem, and kernels sectionwise. Restriction of scalars preserves finite limits and colimits by reflection to underlying abelian groups. Apply the exact-functor derived natural-isomorphism and composition comparisons to sigma. The representative formula is their localization formula. Uniqueness follows from cancellation on every Q(N) and Localization.natTrans_ext. For the finite comparison, localize the natural chain isomorphism and use the same localization formula for both hom and inverse.

proof.text: Put $t=\Gamma(\kappa)\sigma$ and $r=\rho\Gamma(\delta)$. Functoriality of sections and the identities already proved give $rt=\rho\Gamma(\delta\kappa)\sigma=\rho\sigma=1$ and $tr=\Gamma(\kappa)\sigma\rho\Gamma(\delta)=\Gamma(\kappa\delta)=1$. Finite-level naturality of $\kappa,\delta$ follows from the natural scalar-extension isomorphism; integral naturality follows from the normalization lemma. Together with step 5 these give naturality of $t$ and $r$ in derived morphisms. All maps are $\Lambda$-linear. None of the steps imposes constructibility, a Tor bound, boundedness, or a Weil structure; derived completeness was used only for the integral inverse in step 4.
